user_scenario: You are Dana Okonkwo, controller and the authorized contact on file for Merriwether & Pike Accounting, LLC, a 50-person accounting firm in Richmond. It is a hectic Thursday morning and you are phoning Stratton Bay's client services desk about one thing: you want the deposit invoice for the mailbox migration project — the time-and-materials statement of work titled "Microsoft 365 Tenant Consolidation and Mailbox Migration", SOW-043715 — issued today, because your accounts payable run closes this week and you want the deposit in it. You open with exactly that, in plain words; you do not know the deposit amount and you never guess one. You give details one at a time and only when the desk asks: the firm's legal name is Merriwether & Pike Accounting, LLC; your registered phone number is 8045550417; if a second detail is needed, the last four digits of the firm's EIN are 4318 (and, only if those two are somehow not enough, your registered email is dokonkwo@merriwetherpike.com and the support PIN is 427615). If the desk tells you the statement of work has not actually been signed yet, you are surprised — you had assumed it went through after your partners approved the budget — but you are the authorized contact, you can sign it yourself right now, and you say so. When the desk hands the e-signature over to you, you sign it exactly as the desk lays it out: you pass the client reference number, the engagement reference number and the locked rate discount the desk tells you, without changing them, and you read back what the signature confirmation shows if asked. You are content for the desk to post the deposit invoice itself; you are not paying anything on this call — accounts payable will pay it from the invoice — and if the desk offers to take a payment you decline politely. If asked, the scheduled start of November 2 and the planned finish in late March both still suit you, and you have no other changes to the project. If the desk explains how the deposit or the discount was worked out you listen without arguing, since you have no figures of your own to compare. Once the desk tells you the deposit invoice has been posted and gives you its amount, you thank them, say you will forward it to accounts payable, and end the call.
